c.tagline: Taiwan's ancient capital — temple town, historic forts, and street-food soul.

taxi.fareNote: Yellow taxis are metered and cheap and easy to hail in the center; Uber and local apps (LINE Taxi, yoxi) are also widely available.

emergency.note: 110 reaches the police and 119 reaches fire and ambulance; the 24-hour multilingual tourist hotline 0800-011-765 helps foreign visitors.

hood_landmark.Anping District: Anping Old Fort Fort Zeelandia Tainan
hood_landmark.East District (Dong Qu): Blueprint Culture and Creative Park Tainan

hood_desc: The historic heart of Taiwan's oldest city, where Chihkan Tower, the Confucius Temple, and the lantern-lined Shennong Street sit among temples, teahouses, and street-food stalls; the best walkable base for sightseeing.

Tainan's original harbor district, home to Anping Old Fort (Fort Zeelandia), the Anping Tree House, sunset-facing seafood streets, and Old Street snacks; a must-see for history and coastal atmosphere.

The city's modern, youthful quarter around the universities, filled with cafes, boutiques, the Blueprint Culture and Creative Park, and the huge Garden and Dadong night markets; suits shoppers and night-market grazers.
The area around Tainan Railway Station and Tainan Park, a convenient transit gateway with mid-range hotels and easy bus links across the city; handy for arrivals and first nights.
A quieter, more residential and coastal stretch toward Golden Beach and the fishing harbors, away from the tourist crush; good for a relaxed, local-feeling stay.
lodging: Shangri-La Far Eastern Plaza Hotel Tainan

water.note: Tap water is treated but locals boil or filter it; drink boiled or bottled.

transit.hours: Tainan city buses run roughly 6:00 AM to about 10:00-11:00 PM with limited frequency on many routes; there is no metro or tram, so taxis and ride apps cover late nights.
transit.note: Tainan has no metro or tram — the city relies on an extensive but infrequent public bus network (free for the first 8 km with an EasyCard on many routes) plus the T-Bike public bicycle share for short hops; taxis and Uber fill the gaps.
transit.pay: Tap an EasyCard or iPASS stored-value card on buses and T-Bike (buy and top up at any convenience store); many city bus rides are free for the first 8 kilometers with a card. Cash is accepted onboard with exact change.

bus: Tainan Bus Station (Guoguang & Ubus intercity coaches)
train: Tainan HSR Station (Shalun, Taiwan High Speed Rail to Taipei)

transit.m: City bus (Route 5 / Red Line) to Tainan Railway Station (~20 min)
Taxi or Uber to city center (10-15 min)

tip.r: Tipping is not customary in Taiwan; a 10% service charge is sometimes added at hotels and upscale restaurants, but street stalls and taxis expect no tip.
